similarityReviews.rationale: All use a threshold. Withdrawal of invitation, relocating a voice, admitted empty-handed crossing and two nonopening passes have different observable completions.
Remembering the first name, rejecting an imposed role, recognizing the actor as host and separating farewell from greeting have distinct identity conflicts.
Delayed movement copying, changing facial identity and incomplete one-hand reflection use different failures and release actions.
One hand witnessing joined actor palms differs from warming two offered hands with speech and matching a single spread palm. All are negotiated, light and independently supported.
Identifying an actual respondent, stationary environmental listening and reproducing two heard sounds are different observations; none requires supernatural evidence.
Using a newly offered fictional name differs from comparing ordinary and deliberately changed renditions of a phrase. The latter neither asks a name nor reverses words.
The angel’s own actual face releases it; the other actor must lose sight of its reflection behind the rescuer. Existing mirrors are fixed scenery and are never carried, turned or covered.
A returning wrist is stopped by a noncontact barrier, crossed fingers visibly separate, and a hand exits the actor’s body-framed empty space. Full opposing capture actions differ.
Removing an imagined bed, returning an imagined loan, releasing an imagined offering and uncovering a hand-framed shape have different visible endings. All use empty hands.

One actor needs to be admitted to their own place; the other welcomes the rescuer into an absent guest’s place. Taking the place captures in the former and releases in the latter, with different observed social cues.
A single coordinated forward step completing a return differs from an outside orbit around a stationary spinner; neither permits paired exploration.
Two viewpoints on an empty place, an altered ending to a witnessed gesture, and a self-directed release after two visits need no equipment and have distinct completions.

walkthroughs.result: Every possessed release needs at most one free rescuer. P032/P037/P050/P075 have explicit one-hand/light-compatible staging; no second witness, real twin, additional prop holder or external event is required.

New stories introduce no timed revelation, automatic end, forced captive return or role replacement. Repeated acts have rest pauses where needed; each actor may answer real stop/technical speech immediately.
All six prologues use a private dwelling or its grounds. No personal card names a story ID, story cast or a particular fictional event as a prerequisite.

Only people make sounds and move their bodies/phones. Hand-shadow tasks require a real prechecked dim-screen effect. Existing house mirrors are fixed natural features: the angel must actually see its own face. No unseen autonomous object is claimed.

No carried or staged equipment is used. Group members repeat voice/body performance, with pauses as needed. The user permits ordinary existing house mirrors: the angel simply sees its own face; the mirror is not touched. The Dwelling is an agreed empty place.
